Counterexample GX.ThinCex: the model X_alpha = {(p,q) in C^2 : |q| <= 1, |p| = |q|(1-|q|)}, the solid torus C x S^1 with its end collapsed to one point s (a cone over T^2), S_alpha = {s}; G = Z acting on the model geometry X = {0} u devF(C x R) in R x R x C, devF(z,b) = (rho, rho b, z rho e(-rho b^2) - (1-rho)), rho = 1/(1+|z|), by H^n: devF(z,b) -> devF(z,b+n) (faithful, rigid, continuous; X Hausdorff, locally unloopable via a star chart at 0). The (Z,X)-structure of X_alpha is given by the local sections of Q : X -> X_alpha; Sing X_alpha = {s} (the longitude loop has no lift). All hypotheses hold: the family is analytic (every a.e. isomorphism of opens is the identity), X_alpha is locally Galoisian (radial contraction at s), and X_alpha~ carries a tamifying topology with Aut-continuity (X's topology transported by the developing map extended by 0, a bijection; (A) holds because thin tubes saturate under the longitude holonomy: GX.ThinCex.exists_good_shift, GX.ThinCex.CA_subset_Q_Nb; Aut = deck by GX.ThinCex.aeMorphism_XA_unique). So (ii) holds. But the X_A-manifold V = {|q| < 1/2} (an open subset of the model, a collar T^2 x (0,1/2) plus s) is NOT virtually tame (GX.ThinCex.not_isVirtuallyTame_VV): the meridian mu of the collar dies in reg X_alpha but not in reg V; as a deck transformation of V~ it fixes the end over s, D o mu = D, and along any path from z to mu z inside D^{-1}(E), E = {r < 1/4, |w| < 1/4}, the phase Phi = Im w/2pi - r b^2 has cos 2 pi Phi > 0 (it is the argument of w + (1-r)) yet Phi(mu z) = Phi(z) + 1 (the strip argument), contradicting the WP-40c necessary condition GX.not_isVirtuallyTame_of_forall_not_joinedIn.

The proof's gap (l.2130-2134, (D) of r^*T_alpha via lem:spread_top (c)) is not only a gap: piece (2) itself fails for non-descending charts (r : V~ -> V^ not an isomorphism), and no other tamifying topology exists there. The corrected forms remain proved, 0 sorry: descending charts (GX.isVirtuallyTame_of_descending, GX.local_virt_tame_descending), r an isomorphism (GX.isVirtuallyTame_of_hasMaximalLifts), models of finite local degree (GX.isVirtuallyTame_of_isXAManifold_of_hasFiniteLocalDegree), liftable charts (GX.local_virt_tame_liftable); general (ii) => (i) conditional on piece (2) (GX.local_virt_tame_of_charts).

Piece (2) of the proof (the natural local tamifying topologies T_{U,V,phi}, GX.HasLocalTamifyingCharts) is itself false in general: GX.ThinCex.not_forall_hasLocalTamifyingCharts_VV (for V = {|q| < 1/2}, some base point and developing map admit no such family), the contraposition of GX.isVirtuallyTame_of_isXAManifold with GX.ThinCex.isXAManifold_VV and GX.ThinCex.not_isVirtuallyTame_VV (fixer round 1, audit minor 2).

The counterexample's model geometry X is not a manifold at 0 (a point with contractible punctured neighbourhoods); this is allowed by the paper's standing assumption (an analytical structure with X locally unloopable, l.1660; (G,X) analytical, l.341) but is far from the paper's intended (Isom(E^{1,2}), E^{1,2}) setting.
